steps.thought: List all available tests to understand the station capabilities and determine the cheapest tests to run first.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run power_on_selftest as the initial cheap test to quickly enumerate all subsystems and check for any basic communication or boot faults.
steps.observation: The initial power-on self-test passed successfully, with all 4 CAN nodes, UART devices, I2C devices, and camera sensor initialized properly. This rules out major structural boot failures, but comprehensive testing of all subsystems is still required.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power-on self-test passed with no detected faults across system, bus, and boot telemetry. However, functional and load tests must be run on all subsystems before confirming.
There could be subtle degradation in individual subsystems (such as motor bearings, ESC sync, or battery internal resistance) that only appear under load or specific stress tests.

steps.thought: I will run battery_rest_check to check pack and per-cell resting voltages as part of the mandatory subsystem coverage.
steps.observation: The battery rest check passed successfully, showing nominal cell voltages around 4.15V, a healthy pack voltage of 16.6V, and very low cell imbalance of 14mV. This rules out basic battery resting voltage and cell imbalance issues, but full load and subsystem tests are still needed.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power-on self-test and battery rest check passed with no failures. Continuing to test remaining subsystems.
Subsystem faults that only manifest under load or specific conditions have not yet been fully ruled out.

steps.thought: I will run the esc_telemetry test to check for motor and ESC commutation issues since initial boot and battery checks passed.
steps.observation: The ESC telemetry test passed successfully for all four ESCs with zero sync errors, low packet loss, and normal temperatures, ruling out ESC desync or thermal derate issues.

hypotheses.rationale: Power-on selftest, battery rest check, and ESC telemetry have all passed with no failures.
Remaining subsystems such as motors, sensors, harness, compass, and camera still need to be tested.

steps.thought: I will run the compass_static test next to verify compass heading and static behavior, as it is a quick test for the compass subsystem.
steps.observation: The compass_static test passed with a small heading error (-1.52 deg) and normal field magnitude, ruling out static compass hard-iron distortion or sensor failure.

hypotheses.rationale: Power-on selftest, battery rest check, ESC telemetry, and static compass test have all passed successfully.
Remaining subsystems like motors, IMU, camera, harness, and load testing have not yet been evaluated.

steps.thought: I will run the imu_static test to evaluate IMU sensor health and static performance, as this subsystem has not been checked yet.
steps.observation: The imu_static test failed due to an excessive gyro z-axis bias of 1.379 dps, which exceeds the 0.3 dps threshold, while other subsystems checked so far have passed.

hypotheses.rationale: Excessive gyro bias on the z-axis points strongly towards a miscalibrated gyro or calibration offset error.
A loose IMU mount can contribute to abnormal gyro bias or acceleration anomalies.
Failing IMU sensor hardware could manifest as excessive bias, though less common than calibration issues.

steps.thought: Since the IMU static test failed due to excessive gyro z bias, I need to check whether other subsystems (camera, harness, motors, compass under interference, and battery load) have any hidden issues before concluding the diagnosis.
steps.observation: The camera selftest passed successfully with proper frame rate and sensor communication, confirming the camera subsystem is healthy. Combined with the previous imu_static failure showing an excessive gyro z bias, IMU calibration remains the primary root cause candidate.

hypotheses.rationale: Excessive gyro z bias of 1.379 dps strongly points to a calibration offset error.
Mechanical looseness could theoretically cause gyro bias, but calibration is far more likely.
Hardware sensor failure is a remote possibility for high bias.

steps.thought: The imu_static test failed specifically due to high gyro z bias, and all other checked subsystems passed. I will now propose recalibrating the IMU to fix the miscalibration.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: True.

Hardware sensor failure is a remote possibility for high bias.
